plan: Reduce QQQI to 20% to lower concentration and preserve capital.

conservative.read: This conservative approach aims for capital preservation with a target of around 1.5% per month. It significantly reduces risk by cutting all leveraged ETFs and trimming concentrated positions, leading to lower potential drawdowns but also capping upside potential.

plan: Trim QQQI to 25% to balance income and concentration.
Sell SMH to exit a weak semiconductor position.
Trim leveraged ETFs (SOXL, METU, MUU, PLTU, SPAL) to small, controlled allocations.
Buy ERY at 4% as a new, strong risk/reward addition.
This plan seeks risk-first growth by blending broad index, quality tech, and limited leverage.
A moderate cash buffer is maintained, with total adds balanced against trims.
balanced.read: This balanced approach targets around 2.5% per month with a focus on risk-first growth. It reduces leverage and concentration while adding a promising new setup, aiming for a steady growth trajectory with controlled drawdowns.

plan: Trim QQQI slightly to 25% to manage concentration.
Sell SMH to exit a weak semiconductor position.
Add to leveraged ETFs (SOXL, METU, MUU, PLTU, SPAL) to increase exposure.
Buy ERY at 6% as a new, strong risk/reward addition.
This aggressive plan leans into leverage and concentration in high-conviction areas.

aggressive.read: This aggressive strategy targets around 4% per month by increasing leverage and concentrating in high-scoring setups, including leveraged ETFs. It accepts significantly higher potential drawdowns and the risk of rapid losses due to leverage and ETF rebalancing, requiring strict stop discipline.

plan: Increase QQQI to 30% to maximize income generation.
Sell SMH, SOXL, METU, MUU, PLTU, and SPAL to eliminate high-beta and leveraged ETF risk.
This plan prioritizes steady monthly distributions and capital preservation over growth.
Focus shifts to income-generating assets and broad market exposure.

income.read: This income-focused plan targets around 1% per month by prioritizing income-generating assets like QQQI and broad index exposure. It eliminates leveraged and high-beta single names to minimize volatility and maximize reliable monthly distributions, accepting lower growth potential.
